reason: The cited evidence does not address oxygen plasma treatment, self-limiting oxide formation on multi-element alloys, or restructuring mechanisms under exhaust conditions. E1 discusses TMDC alloying for catalytic sites, E2 focuses on Pt sites in HEA for methanol oxidation, and E3 describes a Pd single-atom catalyst on HEFO for diesel oxidation, none of which support the key premises.
premises: Low-temperature oxygen plasma generates reactive oxygen species that induce selective surface oxidation and atom mobility on multi-element alloys.
A thin, self-limiting oxide layer can restructure and stabilize active metal sites without blocking them.
Optimized plasma parameters prevent excessive oxide buildup and preserve catalytic site accessibility.
The treatment protects the surface from sintering and poisoning during low-temperature, transient exhaust operation.
The intervention improves catalytic activity and durability without increasing PGM consumption.
